title: Hidden Assumptions: A Blank Worksheet
html:
Hidden Assumptions: A Blank Worksheet

The chapter reviews and the three design reviews in Appendix B use the same seven fields as this worksheet. Each records an assumption, a test condition, the required constraint, supporting evidence and uncertainty, an observation window, a decision, and its owner.

The completed example below applies those fields to the connection-pool investigation in Chapter 1. Use it to prepare a review of your own application.

Use one entry for one consequential assumption. A proposal may require several entries when capacity, ownership, compatibility, and recovery depend on different evidence or have different owners.

What Each Field Asks For

  1. Assumption and scope. State what must be true for the proposal to work as intended. Identify the request class, resource, instance or region, and configuration where relevant.

  2. Condition that tests it. Describe the workload change, dependency delay, missing response, stale copy, incompatible version, or loss of an owner that could invalidate the assumption.

  3. Constraint or invariant. Identify the resource bound or correctness requirement that must be preserved under that condition.

  4. Evidence and uncertainty. Record the measurement, calculation, experiment, or documented guarantee supporting the decision. State what has not been verified.

  5. Signal and evaluation window. Define the observation that changes the decision, its scope, and its evaluation interval. Include sample requirements and treatment of missing evidence where applicable.

  6. Control and decision. State the automatic control or operator action attached to the condition. Identify the evidence required before resuming or expanding the change.

  7. Owner and review trigger. Name the person or team responsible for the evidence and decision. Identify which changes require another review.

The form of evidence follows the claim. A capacity estimate needs a defined workload and resource boundary. A correctness claim may depend on a transaction rule or guarded state transition. A release decision may require a compatibility test and measurements from a specified evaluation window.

A review can end with a decision to defer release. In that case, an unverified threshold or evaluation interval belongs in the record alongside the evidence needed to establish it. Filling every field with an unsupported number would conceal the work still to be done.

::: hiddenassumptions

Assumption and scope & One Recommendation Service instance can support the proposed product-page workload alongside existing callers using its 40-connection pool.
Condition that tests it & The offered lookup rate reaches 560 per second, connection occupancy increases, or uneven routing assigns more work to one instance.
Constraint or invariant & Assigned connections cannot exceed the pool limit. Acquisition waits must fit the page deadline, and rejected recommendations must permit the base page to complete.
Evidence and uncertainty & At 400 completed lookups per second and 70 ms mean occupancy, average use is 28 connections. At 560 per second, modeled demand is 39.2. A 72 ms mean implies demand above 40. Acceptable operation under that workload has not been established.
Signal and evaluation window & Measure assigned connections, pending acquisitions, acquisition latency, timeouts, and page outcomes per instance and caller. Release thresholds and observation windows require representative load-test evidence before promotion.
Control and decision & Defer further exposure. Validate admission bounds, acquisition timeouts, and a fallback that uses none of the exhausted pool. Approve further exposure only after the workload and stop conditions have been recorded and tested.
Owner and review trigger & The service owner supplies test results. The database owner reviews the shared allocation. The release owner approves exposure. Changes to routing, caller mix, occupancy, or instance count require reassessment.
:::
